uTool.title: Tools (function calling)
uTool.body:
A tool = a name + what it is for + a parameter format; the model writes JSON per the manual and the program actually runs it.

📍 Location: Using agents › Extend it › Tools (function calling)
⚙️ Usage layer: no model parameters change, only how you use it
🧪 Try it:

🎯 Role

  • The manual goes into the context so the model knows the tool exists and how to fill in the parameters.
  • The result comes back to the model as text, and it decides the next step.

▶ How to use it

  • Clear names and descriptions, few parameters; keep read-only tools apart from tools that change things.

🧠 Why it’s designed this way (the logic underneath)

The model only outputs text; agree on a format a program can check, and text can drive any software.

✅ Why this works

If a parameter is wrong, the program sends the error back for the model to fix.

⚠️ Limits / notes: More tools mean longer manuals and more wrong picks.

uMcp.title: MCP (Model Context Protocol)
uMcp.body:
An open protocol proposed in late 2024: any AI app can plug in tools and data that others have built, in one standard way.

📍 Location: Using agents › Extend it › MCP (Model Context Protocol)
⚙️ Usage layer: no model parameters change, only how you use it
🧪 Try it:

🎯 Role

  • Three roles: the host (the AI app you use) → opens one client per server → connected to a server.
  • A server can offer three kinds of things: tools (actions), resources (data to read) and prompt templates.
  • Transports: standard input/output (stdio) locally, HTTP for remote servers.

▶ How to use it

  • Add a server in the app’s settings, then use its tools right in the chat.
  • Connect only servers you trust, and check which permissions they ask for.

🧠 Why it’s designed this way (the logic underneath)

Before, every app had to integrate every tool separately (N×M); with one protocol, each side does it once (N+M).

✅ Why this works

Write a server once and every MCP-capable app can use it.

⚠️ Limits / notes: Server output may carry prompt injections; installing a server means trusting its code and everything it can reach.

uSkill.title: Skills (skill packs)
uSkill.body:
A folder: instructions for “how to do a kind of task” (plus optional scripts and templates); normally only its name and one-line description are shown.

📍 Location: Using agents › Extend it › Skills (skill packs)
⚙️ Usage layer: no model parameters change, only how you use it
🧪 Try it:

🎯 Role

  • Normally: only each skill’s name and description sit in the context, which takes little room.
  • When needed: the agent reads the full instructions and runs the scripts if needed.

▶ How to use it

  • Turn instructions you keep repeating (report format, release steps) into a skill so you never re-explain them.
  • Its scripts get executed: install only skills from trusted sources.

🧠 Why it’s designed this way (the logic underneath)

Tools give hands (actions); skills give know-how (how to do it). Loaded on demand, many skills take little context.

✅ Why this works

The same way of working is reused across a team, so results are more consistent.

⚠️ Limits / notes: With a poor description the agent will not know when to use it; a skill does not teach the model things it fundamentally lacks.
